title: Bernoulli restriction collapses DNF gates to narrow CNFs
statement:
Fix positive integers $n$ and $l$, and let $g_1,\dots,g_{s_i}$ be DNF formulas on $n$ variables, each of width at most $l$, and each in reduced form: no term repeats a literal, and within a term any two literals on the same variable coincide, so every variable occurs at most once in each term. Let $p$ be a real parameter with $0 < p \le 1$ and $p \le \tfrac{1}{40\,l}$. Draw a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction $\rho$ of the $n$ variables, which independently leaves each variable free with probability $p$ and otherwise fixes it to $0$ or $1$ each with probability $(1-p)/2$. Then the probability that some restricted gate fails to be computed by a narrow CNF — that is, for some $i$ there is no CNF formula $\psi$ of width at most $l$ satisfying $\psi(x) = g_i(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ for every assignment $x$ — is at most
\[
  s_i\left(\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{l} + \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{n p}{3}\right)\right).
\]

replaced:
Let $g_1,\dots,g_{s_i}$ be width-$\le l$ DNFs on $n$ variables (with $0<l$,
$0<n$), and let $0<p\le 1/(40l)$ with $p\le 1$. Under a Bernoulli$(p)$ random
restriction $\rho$, the probability that some restricted gate fails to be
representable by a width-$\le l$ CNF agreeing with it pointwise is at most
$s_i\cdot\bigl((1/2)^l+\exp(-np/3)\bigr)$. This is the one-step reduction bound
applied with width parameter $l$.
